title: Real sums of linear thresholds
statement: Let $n$ and $s$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f$ be a Boolean function on $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ with values in $\\{-1,1\\}$. The function $f$ is a real sum of at most $s$ linear threshold functions if there are linear threshold functions $g_1,\\ldots,g_s$ and a real constant $c$ such that, at every input $x$, the real encoding of $f(x)$ equals $c+\\sum_{i=1}^s g_i(x)$, with each $g_i(x)$ interpreted by its real encoding.
